title: AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2: silver-medal level at the Math Olympiad
summary: The two systems solved 4 of 6 problems at IMO 2024, scoring 28 of 42 points, one point below the gold threshold. Problems were manually translated into formal language, and some required up to three days of computation instead of the official 4.5 hours.

evidence.tested: The systems solved official IMO 2024 problems, graded under IMO rules by Prof. Timothy Gowers and Dr Joseph Myers, reaching 28 of 42 points; problems were manually translated into formal language first.
evidence.unknown: Two combinatorics problems remained unsolved, translation was manual, and some solutions took up to three days.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaProof solved three problems with formal proofs, and AlphaGeometry 2 proved the geometry problem within 19 seconds of formalization.

source_review.scope: Original institutional announcement checked for the specific results, AI contribution and limitations cited in the antibiotic dossier or mathematical follow-up pilot. Full-paper reanalysis, external replication and an exhaustive follow-up search were not performed.

relationships.reason: AlphaGeometry 2 is explicitly described as an improved AlphaGeometry version; this link concerns the geometry component, not attribution of all four IMO solutions.

follow_up.note: The updated original announcement dates publication of the AlphaProof methodology in Nature to 12 November 2025. This journal transition is not an independent replication and does not apply to every component of the combined system.

follow_up_review.scope: Bounded check of the original announcements cited by the events recorded here, including explicit links to later program work. This is not an exhaustive literature search or ongoing monitoring commitment.
